name: Chukka boots

card.summary: Ankle-high, two- or three-eyelet leather or suede boots that dress up casual outfits and lengthen the visual line of the leg and shoe.

quick.overview:
Chukka boots are ankle-high lace-up boots with two or three pairs of eyelets, usually in suede or calfskin with a plain rounded toe. People wear them as a step up from sneakers that still reads relaxed.

Their style payoff comes from a clean, uncluttered silhouette that works with jeans, chinos and even suits. The category has a long history in menswear and no clinical research behind it, since it is a clothing choice.
quick.how: Chukkas are worn with jeans, chinos or casual tailoring. Suede versions in tan, brown or navy are common, with leather versions for slightly dressier settings. Soles range from thin leather to crepe or rubber.
quick.risks: Suede marks easily with water and stains, and thin leather soles wear faster than rubber. Fit varies by last and brand, and break-in blisters are possible. No medical risks are documented.

lead: Chukka boots are ankle-high leather boots with open lacing through two or three pairs of eyelets. Uppers are typically suede or calfskin, and soles may be leather, wood or rubber [1].

In appearance terms they give the foot a compact, rounded silhouette that sits between a sneaker and a dress shoe. They can be worn with jeans or with a suit, which is why the style stays popular in menswear, especially in the UK [1].

Shoe historian June Swann describes the essential chukka as ankle-high and unlined, with thin leather soles, two-part calfskin suede uppers and rounded toes. Modern versions resemble Chelsea boots but lace at the front [1]. No clinical studies concern the style.

chain: Ankle-high boot with a clean, rounded shape
angle.text: Chukkas are worn to dress up casual outfits without the formality of lace-up dress shoes. Suede or leather in neutral colours pairs with jeans, chinos or tailoring.

infobox: Two or three pairs of eyelets

paras: The defining features are an ankle-high shaft and open lacing with two or three eyelet pairs. Suede and calfskin uppers are most common, with leather, wooden or rubber soles [1].
The name possibly derives from polo, where a chukka is a period of play. It originally described desert boots worn by British soldiers stationed in India [1].

Clarks' Desert Boot, a type of chukka, debuted at the 1949 Chicago Shoe Fair and was popularised in the 1950s by C. & J. Clark. The company says it was inspired by crepe-soled suede boots made in a Cairo bazaar for British Eighth Army officers. The page links these to the South African veldskoen [1].
The style became popular as casual wear from the late 1940s through the 1960s and remains a staple, worn with suits or with jeans [1].
